title: Morgan Stanley turns cautious on chips
description: The "Halftime Report" traders debate Morgan Stanley's bearish call on the chip sector.

asr.full_text: Welcome back Morgan Stanley telling investors today to cut back on the high flying chip sector they've downgraded it to cautious saying indicators are now flashing red. It's our call of the day. Pete I go to you. You talk about the chips a lot. Risk risk reward poorest. It's been in three years upside to estimates now difficult to come by. I can understand the call. It makes a lot of sense because of the runs that we've seen and there's just just a tremendous run. Give you a great name, Micron, even though it's pulled off of the highs. You still look at the year to date. It's pretty incredible performance. Right. Intel, obviously, there's a lot more going on at Intel than just the business side. And that starts right up at the C-suite at the CEO having to step down. So there are some reasons why I think there are some stocks that are off of their highs. But I would say this. I still think risk-reward-wise the upside looks great. You look at the fundamental story. And I think that there's still plenty of growth. When we look at what are chips really primarily feeding into now when we talk about the major stocks that we talk about. It's AI. It's cloud. It's data centers. It's all of that. And because of that, I still think there's plenty of upside. If you believe in the Microsoft story and the rest of the different cloud names, I think you still have to like some of these chips. They do and they do by the way. I mean they highlight the Overweights they have, NVIDIA and Xilinx. Amberella is where as well as in there so it's not a you know a blanket play on the entire space but as Carrie you noted. Pete said you did have a run. Is it time to move to the sidelines for a bit. So if I were a big chip owner right here having held them perhaps since two thousand and fifteen. That's not our firm. We don't own the chips or the stocks but if I wore and they've gone up five hundred percent six hundred percent some of them I think taking some money off the table is a decent idea just because of the weight must be so big right now. On the other hand, you've got trade to worry about. Nothing to do with price. That could affect sentiment. And, you know, they're a cyclical group. People say they're not cyclical anymore. I don't believe that. They still are cyclical. Taking a little off isn't such a crazy idea. I think they're cyclical in an environment where free cash flow generation is going to continue to accelerate for the technology sector. And I think you're going to see the cloud and IT spending. ANTIDESTIBLE. I THINK YOU'RE GOING TO SEE THE CLOUD IN IT STANDING AND THEY TALK ABOUT IT, BUT THAT ENTERPRISE SPENDING IS GOING TO BE THERE. THEY ALSO TALK ABOUT TRADE RENATIONS WITH THE CHINESE AND THE U.S., AND THAT ACTING AS A and acting as an impediment for further M&A which has been a tailwind for the space, well, that's also making the assumption that there's no resolution to this trade irritant that we have going on. So with a resolution, with free cash flow generation, I do think you could see M&A continue to be present. All right. We haven't seen guys bailing but we have seen guys protecting here, Judge. After this huge run that you spoke of, Carrie, we've seen Western Digital, for instance. End of July, they were aggressively buying puts. They've made a fortune on those puts already. You're going to see the same sort of thing playing out in some of these others. It's not that they're hitting the exits and getting out, but they are protecting. And to Pete's point, you're doing it at a really low VIX right now. I want to bring up another stock before we run. Seagate cut the cell. The stock has been a bum lately. It is down 12 in a half percent. Who has to play on this? My play would be, I still like the fundamentals of the company itself. If you're going off of just this, and not to go right after the analyst, but I have to here because he's the one who's making this call. He's been incorrect almost the entire way in this stock. I mean, we talk about all the time, who do you listen to when it comes to Apple? Who do you listen to when it comes to Amazon? And who do you listen to when it comes to Amazon and Netflix or whatever? And who's really been the best in that space? Unfortunately, the Goldman analyst has not been very correct at all in this particular name so I think for that reason I'm not as concerned about this call
